sentences.zh: 華溫琪

translations.literal: Hua Wenqi
translations.idiomatic: Hua Wenqi

sentences.zh: 華溫琪，字德潤，宋州下邑人也。

translations.literal: Hua Wenqi, courtesy name Derun, was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Wenqi, styled Derun, came from Xiayi in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 世本農家。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers.
translations.idiomatic: His people had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 溫琪身長七尺。

translations.literal: Wenqi stood seven feet in height.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqi stood seven feet tall.

sentences.zh: 少從黃巢為盜，巢陷長安，以溫琪為供奉官都知。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Huang Chao as a bandit; when Chao took Chang’an, he made Wenqi Director of Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he rode with Huang Chao as an outlaw. When Chao seized Chang’an, he made Wenqi Director of Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 巢敗，溫琪走滑州，顧其狀貌魁偉，懼不自容，乃投白馬河，流數十里，不死，河上人援而出之。

translations.literal: When Chao was defeated, Wenqi fled to Huazhou; seeing his stature tall and imposing, fearing he could not hide himself, he threw himself into the Baima River, drifted several tens of li, did not die, and men on the river pulled him out.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fell; Wenqi fled to Huazhou. His frame was huge—he feared he could not hide—and he threw himself into the Baima River. He drifted tens of li, lived, and rivermen hauled him out.

sentences.zh: 又自經於桑林，桑輒枝折。

translations.literal: He again hanged himself in a mulberry grove; the mulberry branches at once broke.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself in a mulberry grove; the branches snapped.

sentences.zh: 乃之胙縣，有田父見之曰：「子狀貌堂堂，非常人也！

translations.literal: He then went to Zuo county; a farmer saw him and said: “Your bearing is stately—you are no ordinary man!
translations.idiomatic: He went to Zuo county. A farmer saw him and said: “Your bearing is stately—you are no ordinary man!

sentences.zh: 」乃匿於家。

translations.literal: ” He was hidden in the man’s home.
translations.idiomatic: ” The farmer hid him at home.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，聞濮州刺史朱裕募士為兵，乃往依之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he heard that Zhu Yu, prefect of Puzhou, was recruiting men for the army, and went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: A year and more later he heard Zhu Yu of Puzhou was recruiting soldiers and went to serve him.

sentences.zh: 後事梁，為開道指揮使，累以戰功為絳、棣二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served Liang as path-clearing commander and, by repeated battle merit, became prefect of Jiang and Di prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Liang as path-clearing commander and, battle after battle, rose to prefect of Jiang and Di.

sentences.zh: 棣州苦河水為患，溫琪徙於新州以避之，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Di prefecture suffered from the Yellow River’s harm; Wenqi moved the people to Xin prefecture to avoid it, and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Di suffered from the Yellow River. Wenqi moved the seat to Xin to escape the floods; the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 歷齊、晉二州。

translations.literal: He served in Qi and Jin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He held Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗攻晉州，逾月不能破，梁末帝嘉溫琪善守，升晉州為定昌軍，以溫琪為節度使。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong attacked Jin prefecture and for more than a month could not take it; Liang’s Last Emperor praised Wenqi’s skill at defense, raised Jin to the Dingchang circuit, and made Wenqi its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong besieged Jin more than a month without breaching it. Liang’s Last Emperor praised Wenqi’s defense, raised Jin to the Dingchang circuit, and made him commissioner.

sentences.zh: 坐掠部民妻，為其夫所訟，罷為金吾衛大將軍、左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: He was removed for seizing a subordinate’s wife, whom her husband sued; he was demoted to Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard and commander of the Left Dragon-Prancing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a subordinate’s wife; the husband sued. He was stripped of his post and made Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard and commander of the Left Dragon-Prancing Army.

sentences.zh: 朱友謙以河中叛附於晉，末帝拜溫琪汝州防禦使、河中行營排陣使。

translations.literal: Zhu Youqian rebelled in Hezhong and joined Jin; the Last Emperor made Wenqi defender of Ruzhou and array-ordering commissioner for the Hezhong field army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian rebelled in Hezhong and went to Jin. The Last Emperor made Wenqi defender of Ru and array-ordering commissioner for the Hezhong campaign.

sentences.zh: 遷耀州觀察留後。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting governor of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting governor of Yao.

sentences.zh: 萇從簡

translations.literal: Chang Congjian
translations.idiomatic: Chang Congjian

sentences.zh: 萇從簡，陳州人也。

translations.literal: Chang Congjian was a native of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Congjian came from Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 世本屠羊。

translations.literal: His family for generations butchered sheep.
translations.idiomatic: His people had butchered sheep for generations.

sentences.zh: 從簡去事晉為軍校，力敵數人，善用槊。

translations.literal: Congjian left to serve Jin as a camp officer; his strength matched several men, and he was skilled with the spear.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian left home to serve Jin as a camp officer. He could match several men in strength and wielded the spear well.

sentences.zh: 莊宗用兵攻城，從簡多為梯頭，莊宗愛其勇，以功累遷步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong used troops to storm cities, Congjian often led the ladder teams; Zhuangzong loved his courage and, by merit, was repeatedly promoted to commander of the foot army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhuangzong’s sieges Congjian often led the ladder teams. Zhuangzong loved his nerve and promoted him step by step to commander of the foot army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與梁軍對陣，梁軍有執大旗出入陣間者，莊宗登高丘望見之，嘆曰：「彼猛士，誰能為我取之者？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong faced the Liang army in battle array; the Liang army had a man carrying a great banner who went in and out of the formation; Zhuangzong climbed a high mound, saw him, and sighed: “That fierce warrior—who can take him for me?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong drew up against Liang. A Liang soldier carried a great banner in and out of the lines. Zhuangzong climbed a knoll, saw him, and sighed: “That brave man—who will take him for me?

sentences.zh: 」從簡因前請往，莊宗惜之，不許。

translations.literal: ” Congjian thereupon stepped forward and asked to go; Zhuangzong cherished him and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congjian stepped forward and volunteered. Zhuangzong cherished him and refused.

sentences.zh: 從簡潛率數騎，馳入梁軍，奪其旗而還，軍中皆鼓噪，莊宗壯之，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: Congjian secretly led several horsemen, galloped into the Liang army, seized their banner, and returned; the whole army cheered, Zhuangzong admired him, and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian stole off with a few horsemen, charged into Liang lines, snatched the banner, and rode back. The host roared; Zhuangzong was thrilled and heaped gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 從簡嘗中流矢，鏃入髀骨，命工取之。

translations.literal: Congjian once took an arrow in flight; the head lodged in his thigh bone, and he ordered a craftsman to extract it.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian once took an arrow; the head lodged in his thigh bone and he called for a surgeon.

sentences.zh: 工無良藥，欲鑿其骨，人皆以為不可。

translations.literal: The craftsman had no good medicine and wished to chisel the bone; everyone said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The surgeon had no good drugs and meant to chisel the bone. Everyone said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 從簡遽使鑿之，工遲疑不忍下，從簡叱其亟鑿，左右視者，皆若不勝其毒，而從簡言笑自若。

translations.literal: Congjian at once had them chisel it; the craftsman hesitated and could not bear to strike down; Congjian shouted at him to chisel quickly; those watching on either side all seemed unable to bear the pain, yet Congjian spoke and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian ordered them to chisel at once. The surgeon hesitated, unable to strike. Congjian roared at him to hurry. Onlookers winced; Congjian talked and laughed as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 然其為人剛暴難制，莊宗每屈法優容之。

translations.literal: Yet as a man he was fierce and violent and hard to control; Zhuangzong each time bent the law and treated him with indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: He was brutal and hard to rein in; Zhuangzong bent the law again and again to indulge him.

sentences.zh: 累遷蔡州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to defender of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to defender of Cai.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，歷麟、汝、汾、金四州防禦使。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he served as defender of Lin, Ru, Fen, and Jin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he held Lin, Ru, Fen, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘗戒之曰：「富貴可惜，然汝不能守也。

translations.literal: Mingzong once admonished him, saying: “Wealth and honor are worth cherishing, yet you cannot keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong once warned him: “Wealth and rank are worth keeping—but you cannot keep them.

sentences.zh: 先帝能貸爾，吾恐不能。

translations.literal: The former emperor could spare you; I fear I cannot.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor could spare you. I may not.

sentences.zh: 」從簡性不可悛，明宗亦不之責。

translations.literal: ” Congjian’s nature could not be changed; Mingzong also did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congjian would not change. Mingzong did not press him.

sentences.zh: 廢帝舉兵於鳳翔，從簡與諸鎮兵圍之，已而兵潰，從簡東走，被執。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor raised troops at Fengxiang, Congjian with the various circuit armies besieged him; before long the army collapsed and Congjian fled east and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Congjian joined the circuit armies to besiege him. The host soon broke; Congjian fled east and was taken.

sentences.zh: 廢帝責其不降，從簡曰：「事主不敢二心。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor reproached him for not surrendering; Congjian said: “In serving one’s lord one dare not harbor a second heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor rebuked him for not yielding. Congjian said: “To serve one’s lord is to serve one lord.

sentences.zh: 」廢帝釋之，拜潁州團練使。

translations.literal: ” The Deposed Emperor released him and made him regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Deposed Emperor freed him and made him regimental commissioner of Ying.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖起兵太原，廢帝將親征，召為招討副使，從至河陽，拜河陽三城節度使。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan, the Deposed Emperor was about to campaign in person; he summoned Congjian as deputy pacification commissioner; Congjian followed to Heyang and was made military commissioner of the Heyang Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Gaozu rose at Taiyuan. The Deposed Emperor meant to march in person, summoned Congjian as deputy pacification commissioner, and took him to Heyang, where he made him commissioner of the Heyang Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 廢帝還洛陽，從簡即降晉。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor returned to Luoyang; Congjian at once surrendered to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor returned to Luoyang; Congjian surrendered to Jin at once.

sentences.zh: 歷鎮忠武、武寧，入為左金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner of Zhongwu and Wuning and entered court as senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He held Zhongwu and Wuning and entered court as senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十五，贈太師。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-five and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 從簡好食人肉，所至多潛捕民間小兒以食。

translations.literal: Congjian loved to eat human flesh; wherever he went he often secretly seized village children to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian ate human flesh. Wherever he served he secretly seized village children for meat.

sentences.zh: 許州富人有玉帶，欲之而不可得，遣二卒夜入其家，殺而取之。

translations.literal: A rich man of Xuzhou had a jade belt; Congjian wanted it but could not obtain it; he sent two soldiers by night into the man’s house to kill him and take it.
translations.idiomatic: A rich man of Xu had a jade belt. Congjian coveted it, could not get it, and sent two soldiers by night to kill the man and seize it.

sentences.zh: 卒夜逾垣，隱木間，見其夫婦相待如賓，二卒嘆曰：「吾公欲奪其寶，而害斯人，吾必不免。

translations.literal: The soldiers by night climbed the wall and hid among the trees; they saw husband and wife treating each other as guests; the two soldiers sighed: “Our lord wants to seize their treasure yet harms such people—we surely will not escape.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers scaled the wall and hid in the trees. Husband and wife treated each other with courtesy. The two sighed: “Our lord wants their treasure and would harm such people—we will not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 」因躍出而告之，使其速以帶獻，遂逾垣而去，不知其所之。

translations.literal: ” They leaped out and told them, urging them quickly to present the belt; then they climbed the wall and left, and no one knew where they went.
translations.idiomatic: ” They sprang out and warned the couple to surrender the belt at once, then vaulted the wall and vanished.

sentences.zh: 張筠

translations.literal: Zhang Yun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun

sentences.zh: （弟抃）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brother Bian appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Younger brother Bian appended)〉

sentences.zh: 張筠，海州人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun was a native of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun came from Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 世以貲為商賈。

translations.literal: His family for generations traded goods as merchants.
translations.idiomatic: His people had been merchants for generations.

sentences.zh: 筠事節度使時溥為宿州刺史。

translations.literal: Yun served the military commissioner Shi Pu as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun served Shi Pu as prefect of Su.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻溥取宿州，得筠，愛其辯惠，以為四鎮客將、長直軍使，累拜宣徽使。

translations.literal: Liang troops attacked Pu and took Suzhou; they obtained Yun, loved his eloquence and cleverness, made him guest officer of the Four Circuits and commander of the Long-Direct Army, and repeatedly promoted him to Palace Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked Pu and took Su. They took Yun, loved his wit, made him guest officer of the Four Circuits and commander of the Long-Direct Army, and raised him to Palace Intendant.

sentences.zh: 末帝分相、澶、衛三州為昭德軍，以筠為節度使，由是魏博軍叛附於晉。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor split Xiang, Chan, and Wei into the Zhaode circuit and made Yun its military commissioner; thereby the Wei-Bo army rebelled and joined Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor carved Xiang, Chan, and Wei into the Zhaode circuit and made Yun commissioner. The Wei-Bo army thereupon rebelled and went to Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉王攻相州，筠棄城走。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin attacked Xiangzhou; Yun abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin attacked Xiang; Yun abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 後以為永平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Later he was made military commissioner of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made commissioner of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 梁亡事唐，仍為京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Liang fell he served Tang and remained as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang fell; he served Tang and remained metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 從郭崇韜伐蜀，為劍南兩川安撫使。

translations.literal: He followed Guo Chongtao in the campaign against Shu as pacification commissioner of the two Shu circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Chongtao against Shu as pacification commissioner of the two Shu circuits.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，拜河南尹，徙鎮興元。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was made metropolitan governor of Henan and transferred to hold Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pacified, he was made metropolitan governor of Henan, then transferred to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 筠嘗有疾，不見將吏，副使符彥琳入問疾，筠又辭不見。

translations.literal: Yun once fell ill and would not see generals or clerks; the deputy Fu Yanlin entered to inquire after his illness, and Yun again declined to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun once fell ill and refused to see generals or clerks. Deputy Fu Yanlin came to inquire; Yun refused again.

sentences.zh: 彥琳疑筠已死，即請出牌印。

translations.literal: Yanlin suspected Yun was already dead and at once asked to take out the tally seal.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlin suspected Yun was dead and asked for the tally seal.

sentences.zh: 筠怒，命左右收彥琳下獄，以其反聞。

translations.literal: Yun in anger ordered his attendants to seize Yanlin and imprison him, and reported his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yun in fury had attendants seize Yanlin and throw him in prison, then reported him for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 明宗知彥琳無反狀，召彥琳釋之，陽徙筠為西京留守，戒守者不內，筠至長安不得入，乃朝京師，以為左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Mingzong knew Yanlin had no rebellious intent; he summoned Yanlin and released him, ostensibly transferred Yun to western capital custodian, warned the guards not to admit him; Yun reached Chang’an and could not enter, then went to court at the capital and was made senior general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong knew Yanlin was no rebel. He summoned Yanlin and freed him, moved Yun ostensibly to western capital custodian, and told the guards not to let him in. Yun reached Chang’an and could not enter; he went to the capital and was made senior general of the Left Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 筠弟抃，當筠為京兆尹時，以為牙內指揮使、三白渠營田制置使。

translations.literal: Yun’s younger brother Bian, when Yun was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was made commander of the inner guard and commissioner for the Three White Canal military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Yun’s younger brother Bian, while Yun was governor of Jingzhao, was made commander of the inner guard and commissioner for the Three White Canal colonies.

sentences.zh: 筠西伐蜀，留抃守京兆。

translations.literal: When Yun campaigned west against Shu he left Bian to hold Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yun marched west against Shu and left Bian to hold Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，魏王繼岌班師，至興平，而明宗自魏起，京師大亂，抃乃斷咸陽浮橋以拒繼岌，繼岌乃自殺。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified the Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew the army; reaching Xingping, Mingzong rose from Wei and the capital fell into great disorder; Bian then cut the Xianyang floating bridge to block Jiji, and Jiji thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pacified, Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew. At Xingping Mingzong rose from Wei and the capital erupted. Bian cut the Xianyang floating bridge to block Jiji; Jiji killed himself.

sentences.zh: 初，筠代康懷英為永平軍節度使，而懷英死，筠即掠其家貲。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yun replaced Kang Huaiying as military commissioner of Yongping and Huaiying died, Yun at once plundered his household goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun replaced Kang Huaiying as commissioner of Yongping and Huaiying died, Yun looted his household at once.

sentences.zh: 又於唐故宮掘地，多得金玉。

translations.literal: He also dug in the ground of the old Tang palace and obtained much gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: He dug in the old Tang palace grounds and found much gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 有偏將侯莫陳威者，嘗與溫韜發唐諸陵，分得寶貨，筠因以事殺威而取之。

translations.literal: There was a deputy general Hou Mo Chenwei who had once with Wen Tao opened the Tang tombs and divided the treasures; Yun on that account killed Wei and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Hou Mo Chenwei had once joined Wen Tao in opening the Tang tombs and splitting the treasure. Yun killed him on that pretext and took the hoard.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌死渭南，抃悉取其行橐。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wei Jiji died at Weinan, Bian took all his traveling baggage.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wei Jiji died at Weinan, Bian seized all his traveling baggage.

sentences.zh: 而王衍自蜀行至秦川，莊宗遣宦者向延嗣殺之，延嗣因盡得衍蜀中珍寶。

translations.literal: Wang Yan of Shu was being escorted to Qinchuan when Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to kill him; Yansi thereby obtained all of Yan’s Shu treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan of Shu was marched toward Qinchuan when Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to kill him; Yansi took all Yan’s Shu treasures.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，即遣人捕誅宦者，延嗣亡命，而蜀之珍寶抃又取之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he at once sent men to seize and execute the eunuchs; Yansi fled, and Bian again took the Shu treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong took the throne and sent men to hunt down the eunuchs. Yansi fled; Bian took the Shu treasures again.

sentences.zh: 由是兄弟貲皆巨萬。

translations.literal: Thereby the brothers’ wealth each reached tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers’ wealth each ran to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 然筠為人好施予，以其富，故所至不為聚斂，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Yet Yun as a man loved to give; because he was wealthy, wherever he went he did not practice heavy exactions, and the people relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yun loved to give. Rich as he was, he did not squeeze the people wherever he served, and they lived easier for it.

sentences.zh: 而抃嗜酒貪鄙，歷沂、密二州刺史。

translations.literal: Bian was addicted to wine, greedy, and base, and served as prefect of Yi and Mi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Bian drank hard, was greedy and base, and held Yi and Mi.

sentences.zh: 晉出帝時，以將軍市馬於回鶻，坐馬不中式，有司理其價直，抃性鄙，因郁郁而卒。

translations.literal: Under Jin’s Outgoing Emperor he went as a general to buy horses from the Uyghurs; because the horses did not meet standard, the authorities assessed their value; Bian’s nature was base, and he therefore died in gloom.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Outgoing Emperor he went as a general to buy horses from the Uyghurs. The horses failed inspection; the authorities charged him the price. Mean by nature, he sickened and died of spite.

sentences.zh: 筠居洛陽，擁其貲，以酒色聲妓自娛足者十餘年，人謂之「地仙。

translations.literal: Yun lived in Luoyang, amassed his wealth, and for more than ten years satisfied himself with wine, women, and singing girls; people called him “earth immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Yun lived in Luoyang, hoarded his wealth, and for more than ten years drowned himself in wine, women, and song; people called him an “earth immortal.

sentences.zh: 」天福二年，徙居長安。

translations.literal: ” In the second year of Tianfu he moved to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Tianfu 2 he moved to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 是歲，張從賓作亂，入洛陽，筠遂以免。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Congbin rebelled and entered Luoyang; Yun thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Congbin rebelled and entered Luoyang; Yun escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，五代反者多矣，吾於明宗獨難其辭。

translations.literal: Alas, in the Five Dynasties there were many rebels; I alone find it hard to speak of Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—in the Five Dynasties rebels were many; I alone find it hard to judge Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 至於魏王繼岌薨，然後終其事也。

translations.literal: Only when Prince of Wei Jiji died was the matter finally concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Prince of Wei Jiji died was the affair finally settled.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遇弒，繼岌以元子握重兵，死於外而不得立，此大事也，而前史不書其所以然。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong met assassination; Jiji as eldest son held heavy troops, died abroad and could not ascend—this was a great affair, yet the earlier histories do not record why it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was murdered. Jiji, the eldest son, held the main army, died abroad, and never took the throne—a great matter—yet earlier histories never say why.

sentences.zh: 夫繼岌之存亡，於張抃無所利害，抃何為而拒之不使之東乎？

translations.literal: Whether Jiji lived or died was of no profit or harm to Zhang Bian—why did Bian block him and not let him march east?
translations.idiomatic: Jiji’s life or death meant nothing to Zhang Bian—why did Bian bar him and refuse to let him march east?

sentences.zh: 豈其有所使而為之乎？

translations.literal: Was someone perhaps using him to do it?
translations.idiomatic: Had someone set him to it?

sentences.zh: 然明宗於符彥超深以為德，而待抃無所厚，此其又可疑也。

translations.literal: Yet Mingzong deeply credited Fu Yanchao with virtue, yet treated Bian without special favor—this too is doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong deeply credited Fu Yanchao with virtue, yet showed Bian no special favor—here too one may doubt.

sentences.zh: 不然，好亂之臣，望風而饗應乎？

translations.literal: If not, was it that men who love disorder answer the wind with a feast?
translations.idiomatic: If not, do men who love chaos answer every wind with a feast?

sentences.zh: 使抃不斷浮橋，而繼岌得以兵東，明宗未必能自立。

translations.literal: Had Bian not cut the floating bridge and Jiji been able to bring his army east, Mingzong might not have been able to stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Had Bian not cut the bridge and Jiji marched east with his army, Mingzong might never have held his own.

sentences.zh: 則繼岌之死，由抃之拒，其所系者豈小哉！

translations.literal: Then Jiji’s death came from Bian’s refusal—how could what hung on it be small!
translations.idiomatic: Jiji died because Bian barred him—the stakes were not small.

sentences.zh: 楊彥詢

translations.literal: Yang Yanxun
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanxun

sentences.zh: 楊彥詢，字成章，河中寶鼎人也。

translations.literal: Yang Yanxun, courtesy name Chenzhang, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanxun, styled Chenzhang, came from Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少事青州王師範，師範好學，聚書萬卷，使彥詢掌之。

translations.literal: In youth he served Wang Shifan of Qingzhou; Shifan loved learning, amassed ten thousand scrolls of books, and had Yanxun keep them.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he served Wang Shifan of Qingzhou. Shifan loved learning, kept ten thousand scrolls, and put Yanxun in charge of them.

sentences.zh: 彥詢為人聰悟，遂見親信。

translations.literal: Yanxun was clever and perceptive and thereupon won close trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun was quick-witted and won his trust.

sentences.zh: 師範降梁，後見殺，彥詢無所歸，乃之魏，事楊師厚為客將。

translations.literal: Shifan surrendered to Liang and later was killed; Yanxun had nowhere to go, went to Wei, and served Yang Shihou as guest officer.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan surrendered to Liang and was later killed. Yanxun had nowhere to turn; he went to Wei and served Yang Shihou as guest officer.

sentences.zh: 魏博叛梁入於晉，彥詢因留事晉。

translations.literal: When Wei-Bo rebelled against Liang and entered Jin, Yanxun therefore remained to serve Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei-Bo rebelled against Liang and went to Jin, Yanxun stayed to serve Jin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁，以彥詢為引進副使，奉使吳、蜀，常稱旨。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he made Yanxun deputy introducing commissioner; as envoy to Wu and Shu he often pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and made Yanxun deputy introducing commissioner. As envoy to Wu and Shu he often pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 歷德州刺史、羽林將軍晉高祖鎮太原，廢帝疑其有貳誌，擇諸將之謹厚者佐之，乃以彥詢為太原節度副使。

translations.literal: Having served as prefect of Dezhou and general of the Feathered Forest, when Jin Gaozu held Taiyuan, Emperor Fei suspected he harbored divided loyalty, chose the most careful and honest among the generals to assist him, and made Yanxun deputy military commissioner of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had been prefect of De and general of the Feathered Forest. When Jin Gaozu held Taiyuan, Emperor Fei suspected divided loyalty and chose the steadiest generals to assist him—Yanxun became deputy commissioner of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其後晉高祖以疑見徙，欲拒命不行，以問彥詢，彥詢不敢正言，因曰：「太原之力，能與唐敵否？

translations.literal: Later Jin Gaozu was transferred on suspicion and wished to refuse the order and not go; he asked Yanxun, and Yanxun dared not speak plainly, and therefore said: “Can Taiyuan’s strength match Tang’s?
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin Gaozu was moved on suspicion and meant to refuse and not go. He asked Yanxun. Yanxun dared not speak plainly and said: “Can Taiyuan’s strength match Tang’s?

sentences.zh: 公其審計之！

translations.literal: My lord, weigh it carefully!
translations.idiomatic: My lord—weigh it carefully!

sentences.zh: 」高祖反意已決，彥詢亦不復敢言。

translations.literal: ” Gaozu’s intent to rebel was already fixed, and Yanxun also no longer dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gaozu’s mind to rebel was set; Yanxun dared say no more.

sentences.zh: 高祖左右以彥詢異議，欲殺之，高祖遽止之，曰：「惟副使一人，我自保之。

translations.literal: Gaozu’s attendants, because Yanxun had voiced a different opinion, wished to kill him; Gaozu hurriedly stopped them, saying: “There is only the one deputy commissioner—I will protect him myself.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s attendants, because Yanxun had disagreed, wanted him killed. Gaozu stopped them at once: “He is my only deputy—I will protect him myself.

sentences.zh: 」乃免。

translations.literal: ” and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was spared.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖乞兵於契丹，契丹耶律德光立高祖於太原，以兵送至河上。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu begged troops from the Khitan; the Khitan Yelü Deguang set Gaozu on the throne at Taiyuan and escorted him with troops to the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozu begged troops from the Khitan. Yelü Deguang set him on the throne at Taiyuan and escorted him with an army to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 彥詢為宣徽使，數往來虜帳中，德光亦愛其為人。

translations.literal: Yanxun was Palace Secretariat commissioner and often went back and forth in the barbarians’ camp; Deguang also loved his character.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun was Palace Secretariat commissioner and often shuttled in the Khitan camp. Deguang also took to his character.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜威德軍節度使，復入為宣徽使，又拜安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next year he was made military governor of the Weide army, again entered as Palace Secretariat commissioner, and was again made military governor of the Anguo army.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took Weide, returned as Palace Secretariat commissioner, and was again made military governor of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 天福七年，徙鎮鎮國，遭歲大饑，為政有惠愛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu he was shifted to govern Zhenguo; the year saw great famine, and his rule was kindly.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 7 he was moved to Zhenguo. Famine struck that year, yet his rule was kindly.

sentences.zh: 以病風罷為右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Stricken with wind illness he was removed as senior general of the Right Golden Crow guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wind illness forced him out as senior general of the Right Golden Crow guard.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy-four and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four, posthumously Grand Preceptor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 李周，字通理，邢州內丘人，唐昭義軍節度使抱真之後也。

translations.literal: Li Zhou, style name Tongli, was a man of Neiqiu in Xingzhou, a descendant of Tang’s Zhaoyi army military governor Bao Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou, style name Tongli, came from Neiqiu in Xingzhou—a descendant of Tang’s Zhaoyi military governor Bao Zhen.

sentences.zh: 父矩，遭世亂不仕，嘗謂周曰：「邯鄣用武之地，今世道未平，汝當從軍旅以興吾門。

translations.literal: His father Ju, meeting the age’s turmoil, did not take office; he once told Zhou: “Handan is a battlefield; the age is not yet settled—you should join the army to raise our house.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju, in the age’s turmoil, held no office. He once told Zhou: “Handan is a battlefield and the world is not settled. You should take to the army and raise our house.

sentences.zh: 」周年十六，為內丘捕賊將，以勇聞。

translations.literal: ” At sixteen Zhou became Neiqiu bandit-catcher captain and was known for courage.
translations.idiomatic: ” At sixteen Zhou became Neiqiu bandit-catcher captain and was known for courage.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁、晉兵爭山東，群盜充斥道路，行者必以兵衛。

translations.literal: At that time Liang and Jin armies contested Shandong; bandits filled the roads, and travelers had to travel under arms.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jin were fighting over Shandong. Bandits choked the roads; every traveler went under arms.

sentences.zh: 內丘人盧嶽將徙家太原，舍逆旅，傍徨不敢進，周意憐之，為送至西山。

translations.literal: The Neiqiu man Lu Yue was about to move his household to Taiyuan, lodged at an inn, and hovered afraid to go on; Zhou pitied him and escorted him to the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue of Neiqiu was moving his household to Taiyuan, stopped at an inn, and dared not go on. Zhou pitied him and saw him to the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 有盜從林中射嶽，中其馬，周大呼曰：「吾在此，孰敢爾邪？

translations.literal: Bandits shot Yue from the woods and hit his horse; Zhou shouted: “I am here—who dares touch him?
translations.idiomatic: Bandits shot from the woods and hit Yue’s horse. Zhou shouted: “I am here—who dares touch him?

sentences.zh: 」盜聞其聲，曰：「此李周也。

translations.literal: ” The bandits heard his voice and said: “That is Li Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” The bandits heard him and said: “That is Li Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」因各潰去。

translations.literal: ” and each scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: ” and each scattered.

sentences.zh: 周送嶽至太原，嶽謂之曰：「吾少學星歷，且工相人。

translations.literal: Zhou escorted Yue to Taiyuan; Yue told him: “In youth I studied the stars and am skilled at reading faces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou saw Yue to Taiyuan. Yue said: “In youth I studied the stars and read faces.

sentences.zh: 子方頤隆準，眉目疏徹，身長七尺，真將相也。

translations.literal: You have a broad forehead and high nose, clear brows and eyes, and stand seven feet—a true minister or general.
translations.idiomatic: You have a broad forehead, high nose, clear brows and eyes, and stand seven feet—a born minister or general.

sentences.zh: 吾占天象，晉必有天下，子宜留事晉，以圖富貴。

translations.literal: I read the heavens: Jin must have the realm. You should stay and serve Jin to win wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: I read the heavens: Jin must take the realm. Stay and serve Jin for wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 」周以母老辭歸。

translations.literal: ” Zhou, citing his aged mother, declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhou pleaded an aged mother and went home.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁遣葛從周攻下邢、洺，晉王柵兵青山口，周未知所歸，乃思嶽言，至青山歸晉，晉王以周為萬勝黃頭軍使。

translations.literal: At that time Liang sent Ge Congzhou to take Xing and Mo; the Prince of Jin barred troops at Qingshan Pass. Zhou did not know where to turn, recalled Yue’s words, went to Qingshan and submitted to Jin; the Prince of Jin made him Wan Sheng Yellow-Head army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Ge Congzhou against Xing and Mo; the Prince of Jin barred Qingshan Pass. Zhou, unsure where to turn, recalled Yue’s words, went to Qingshan and joined Jin. The Prince made him Wan Sheng Yellow-Head army commander.

sentences.zh: 後從征伐常有功。

translations.literal: Later in campaigns he often had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In later campaigns he often won merit.

sentences.zh: 從戰柏鄉，先登，遷匡霸指揮使，守楊劉。

translations.literal: At the battle of Baixiang he was first up the wall; he was made Kuangba army commander and garrisoned Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: At Baixiang he was first over the wall. He was made Kuangba army commander and garrisoned Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 周為將甚勇，其於用兵，善守，能與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: Zhou as a general was very brave; in using troops he was good at defense and could share hardship with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was a bold general, skilled in defense, who shared hardship with his men.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻周，周堅守。

translations.literal: Liang troops attacked Zhou; Zhou held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked Zhou. Zhou held firm.

sentences.zh: 久之，周聞母喪奔歸，莊宗遣佗將代周守，幾為梁兵所破，莊宗遽追周還守之，乃得不破。

translations.literal: After a long while Zhou heard his mother had died and rushed home; Zhuangzong sent another general to replace Zhou in the defense, and the place was nearly taken by Liang troops; Zhuangzong hurriedly recalled Zhou to hold it again, and only then was it not lost.
translations.idiomatic: Long after, Zhou heard his mother had died and rushed home. Zhuangzong sent another to hold Yangliu; Liang nearly took it. Zhuangzong recalled Zhou at once, and the post held.

sentences.zh: 其後梁人已破德勝，因東擊楊劉，以巨艦絕河，斷晉餉援。

translations.literal: Later Liang troops had broken Desheng and then struck east at Yangliu, using great ships to block the river and cut Jin’s supply line.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had taken Desheng and struck east at Yangliu with great ships across the river, cutting Jin’s supplies.

sentences.zh: 周遣人馳趨莊宗求救，請日行百里以赴急，莊宗笑曰：「周為我守，何憂！

translations.literal: Zhou sent a man galloping to Zhuangzong for rescue, asking to march a hundred li a day for the emergency; Zhuangzong laughed and said: “Zhou holds for me—what worry!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent a rider galloping to Zhuangzong for rescue, begging a hundred li a day. Zhuangzong laughed: “Zhou holds for me—what worry!

sentences.zh: 」日行六十里，且行且獵，曰：「周非梁將可敵也。

translations.literal: ” He marched sixty li a day, hunting as he went, and said: “Zhou is not a match for any Liang general.
translations.idiomatic: ” He marched sixty li a day, hunting on the road, and said: “No Liang general can stand against Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」比至，周已絕糧三日。

translations.literal: ” When he arrived, Zhou had been without grain three days.
translations.idiomatic: ” When he arrived, Zhou had been without grain three days.

sentences.zh: 莊宗以巨筏積薪沃油，順流縱火焚梁艦，梁兵解去。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong with great rafts piled fuel, poured oil, and sent fire downstream to burn Liang’s ships; Liang troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong built great rafts, piled fuel, poured oil, and sent fire downstream to burn Liang’s fleet. Liang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 莊宗見周勞曰：「微公，諸將為梁擒矣！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong met Zhou and praised him, saying: “Without you, the generals would have been taken by Liang!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong met Zhou and praised him: “Without you, the generals would have been Liang’s prisoners!

sentences.zh: 」歷相、蔡二州刺史。

translations.literal: ” He served in succession as prefect of Xiang and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: ” He served in turn as prefect of Xiang and Cai.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，拜武信軍節度使，徙鎮靜難，歷武寧、安遠、永興、宣武四鎮，所至多善政。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he was made military governor of Wuxin, shifted to Jingnan, and held in succession Wuning, Anyuan, Yongxing, and Xuanwu—wherever he went his rule was largely good.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he took Wuxin, then Jingnan, and in turn Wuning, Anyuan, Yongxing, and Xuanwu—wherever he went, rule was largely good.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，復鎮靜難，罷還。

translations.literal: Under Jin’s Gaozu he again held Jingnan and was removed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Gaozu he again held Jingnan, then was recalled.

sentences.zh: 出帝幸澶淵，以周留守東京，還，拜開封尹。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor went to Chanyuan, Zhou was left to guard the Eastern Capital; on his return he was made Kaifeng intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor went to Chanyuan, Zhou stayed to guard the Eastern Capital. On return he was made Kaifeng intendant.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四，贈太師。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy-four and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four, posthumously Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 劉處讓

translations.literal: Liu Churang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Churang

sentences.zh: 劉處讓，字德謙，滄州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Churang, style name Deqian, was a man of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Churang, style name Deqian, came from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為張萬進親吏，萬進入梁，為泰寧軍節度使，以處讓為牙將。

translations.literal: In youth he was a personal clerk to Zhang Wanjin; Wanjin entered Liang and became military governor of the Taining army, making Churang a yajun officer.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was Zhang Wanjin’s personal clerk. Wanjin entered Liang as Taining military governor and made Churang a yajun officer.

sentences.zh: 萬進叛梁附晉，梁遣劉鄩討之。

translations.literal: Wanjin rebelled against Liang and joined Jin; Liang sent Liu Yun to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin rebelled against Liang for Jin. Liang sent Liu Yun against him.

sentences.zh: 萬進遣處讓求救於晉，晉王方與梁相拒，未能出兵，處讓乃於軍門截耳而訴曰：「萬進所以見圍者，以附晉故也，奈何不顧其急？

translations.literal: Wanjin sent Churang to Jin for rescue; the Prince of Jin was just facing Liang and could not send troops. Churang then at the army gate cut off his ear and pleaded: “Wanjin is besieged because he joined Jin—why not heed his peril?
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin sent Churang to beg Jin for rescue. The Prince of Jin was locked with Liang and could not march. Churang cut off his ear at the army gate and pleaded: “Wanjin is besieged for joining you—why ignore his peril?

sentences.zh: 茍不出兵，願請死！

translations.literal: If you will not march, I beg to die!
translations.idiomatic: If you will not march, I beg to die!

sentences.zh: 」晉王壯之，曰：「義士也！

translations.literal: ” The Prince of Jin was stirred and said: “A man of righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Prince was stirred: “A man of righteousness!

sentences.zh: 」為之發兵。

translations.literal: ” and sent troops for him.
translations.idiomatic: ” and sent troops.

sentences.zh: 未渡河，而萬進為梁兵所敗，處讓因留事晉。

translations.literal: Before crossing the river Wanjin was defeated by Liang troops; Churang therefore stayed to serve Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army crossed the river Wanjin was beaten by Liang. Churang stayed with Jin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，為客省使，常使四方，多稱旨。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was made guest-reception commissioner, often sent to the four quarters, and often won approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was guest-reception commissioner, often sent abroad, and often pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 天成中，遷引進使，累遷左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was promoted to introduction commissioner and in succession to Left Awesome Guard senior general.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng he rose to introduction commissioner and in turn to Left Awesome Guard senior general.

sentences.zh: 廢帝時，魏州軍亂，逐其帥劉延皓，遣範延光招討，以處讓為河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor Wei prefecture’s army mutinied, drove its commander Liu Yanhao, and Fan Yan’guang was sent to pacify them; Churang was made overall transport commissioner for Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor Wei’s army mutinied, drove Liu Yanhao, and Fan Yan’guang was sent to pacify them. Churang was made overall Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖立，歷宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: When Jin’s Gaozu took the throne he served in succession as Southern Court Palace Secretariat commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s Gaozu rose he served in turn as Southern Court Palace Secretariat commissioner.

sentences.zh: 範延光反，高祖命楊光遠為招討使，以處讓參其軍事。

translations.literal: Fan Yan’guang rebelled; Gaozu appointed Yang Guangyuan pacification commissioner and had Churang join his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yan’guang rebelled. Gaozu made Yang Guangyuan pacification commissioner and put Churang on his staff.

sentences.zh: 已而副招討使張從賓叛於河陽，處讓分兵擊破從賓。

translations.literal: Before long the deputy pacification commissioner Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang; Churang divided troops and broke Congbin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon deputy pacification commissioner Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang. Churang split forces and broke him.

sentences.zh: 還，與光遠攻鄴，逾年不能下。

translations.literal: Returning, he with Guangyuan attacked Ye; more than a year passed and they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he and Guangyuan besieged Ye for more than a year without success.

sentences.zh: 其後延光有降意而遲疑，處讓入城，譬以禍福，延光乃出降。

translations.literal: Later Yan’guang wished to surrender but hesitated; Churang entered the city and urged him with fortune and ruin, and Yan’guang then came out in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan’guang wished to surrender but wavered. Churang entered the city, urged fortune and ruin, and Yan’guang came out in surrender.

sentences.zh: 唐制，樞密使常以宦者為之，自梁用敬翔、李振，至莊宗始用武臣，而權重將相，高祖時，以宰相桑維翰、李崧兼樞密使，處讓與諸宦者心不平之。

translations.literal: Tang’s system often had eunuchs as Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners; from Liang’s use of Jing Xiang and Li Zhen, through Zhuangzong’s first use of military officers, their power weighed on generals and ministers. Under Gaozu the chancellors Sang Weihan and Li Song also held the Bureau post; Churang and the other eunuchs were resentful in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Tang usually put eunuchs in the Bureau of Military Affairs. Liang used Jing Xiang and Li Zhen; Zhuangzong first used military men, and their power weighed on generals and ministers. Under Gaozu chancellors Sang Weihan and Li Song also held the Bureau. Churang and the other eunuchs seethed.

sentences.zh: 光遠之討延光也，以晉重兵在己掌握，舉動多驕恣，其所求請，高祖頗裁抑之。

translations.literal: When Guangyuan campaigned against Yan’guang he held Jin’s main forces in his grasp and his conduct was often arrogant; what he asked for Gaozu often trimmed.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Yan’guang, Guangyuan held Jin’s main forces and grew arrogant. Gaozu often trimmed his requests.

sentences.zh: 處讓為光遠言：「此非上意，皆維翰、崧等嫉公耳！

translations.literal: Churang told Guangyuan: “This is not the emperor’s mind—it is all Sang Weihan, Li Song, and the rest who envy you!
translations.idiomatic: Churang told Guangyuan: “That is not the throne’s mind—Sang Weihan, Li Song, and the rest envy you!

sentences.zh: 」光遠大怒。

translations.literal: ” Guangyuan was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: ” Guangyuan flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 及兵罷，光遠見高祖，訴以維翰等沮己，高祖不得已，罷維瀚等，以處讓為樞密使。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended Guangyuan saw Gaozu and complained that Weihan and the rest had blocked him; Gaozu had no choice but to remove Weihan and the rest and make Churang Bureau commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended Guangyuan saw Gaozu and charged that Weihan and the rest had blocked him. Gaozu had no choice: he removed Weihan and the rest and made Churang Bureau commissioner.

sentences.zh: 處讓在職，凡所陳述，多不稱旨。

translations.literal: In office, whatever Churang presented rarely pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In office, little Churang said pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 處讓丁母憂，高祖遂不復拜樞密使，以其印付中書而廢其職。

translations.literal: Churang entered mourning for his mother; Gaozu then never again appointed a Bureau commissioner, gave its seal to the Secretariat, and abolished the office.
translations.idiomatic: Churang mourned his mother. Gaozu never again appointed a Bureau commissioner, handed its seal to the Secretariat, and abolished the post.

sentences.zh: 處讓居喪期年，起復為彰德軍節度使、右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: After a year in mourning Churang was recalled to serve as Zhangde army military governor and Right Golden Crow guard senior general.
translations.idiomatic: After a year’s mourning he was recalled as Zhangde military governor and Right Golden Crow senior general.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，年六十三，累贈太師。

translations.literal: He died of illness aged sixty-three and was repeatedly posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at sixty-three, repeatedly posthumously Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 李承約

translations.literal: Li Chengyue
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengyue

sentences.zh: 李承約，字德儉，薊門人也。

translations.literal: Li Chengyue, style name Dejian, was a man of Jimen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengyue, style name Dejian, came from Jimen.

sentences.zh: 少事劉仁恭，為山後八軍巡檢使，將騎兵二千人。

translations.literal: In youth he served Liu Rengong as inspector of the eight armies behind the mountains, commanding two thousand horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Liu Rengong as inspector of the eight armies behind the mountains with two thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 仁恭為其子守光所囚，承約以其騎兵奔晉，晉王以為匡霸指揮使。

translations.literal: Rengong was imprisoned by his son Shouguang; Chengyue fled to Jin with his horse; the Prince of Jin made him Kuangba army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was imprisoned by his son Shouguang. Chengyue fled to Jin with his horse. The Prince made him Kuangba army commander.

sentences.zh: 從破夾寨，戰臨清，以功累遷洺汾二州刺史、潁州團練使。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking the stockade fort and fought at Linqing; for merit he rose in succession to prefect of Mo and Fen and regimental commissioner of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He helped break the stockade fort and fought at Linqing. For merit he rose to prefect of Mo and Fen and regimental commissioner of Ying.

sentences.zh: 天成中，邠州節度使毛璋有異志，明宗拜承約涇州節度副使，使往伺璋動靜。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era Bin prefecture’s military governor Mao Zhang harbored divergent intent; Mingzong made Chengyue deputy military governor of Jing and sent him to watch Zhang’s movements.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng Bin’s military governor Mao Zhang showed divergent intent. Mingzong made Chengyue Jing deputy governor and sent him to watch Zhang.

sentences.zh: 承約見璋，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Chengyue saw Zhang and urged him with fortune and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyue saw Zhang and urged fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 後明宗遣人代璋，璋即時受代。

translations.literal: Later Mingzong sent a man to replace Zhang; Zhang at once accepted replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mingzong sent a man to replace Zhang, and Zhang accepted replacement at once.

sentences.zh: 明宗大喜，即拜承約黔南節度使。

translations.literal: Mingzong was greatly pleased and at once made Chengyue military governor of Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was pleased and at once made Chengyue Qiannan military governor.

sentences.zh: 承約以恩信撫諸夷落，勸民農桑，興起學校。

translations.literal: Chengyue with kindness and trust soothed the various barbarian tribes, urged the people in farming and sericulture, and raised schools.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyue soothed the tribes with kindness and trust, urged farming and sericulture, and raised schools.

sentences.zh: 居數年，當代，黔南人詣京師乞留，為許留一年。

translations.literal: After several years, when his term ended, Qiannan people went to the capital begging he stay; he was allowed one more year.
translations.idiomatic: After several years his term ended. Qiannan people went to the capital begging he stay, and one more year was granted.

sentences.zh: 召為左衛上將軍，改左龍武統軍，拜昭義軍節度使，復為左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Guard senior general, changed to Left Dragon Martial army commander, made Zhaoyi army military governor, and again made Left Dragon Martial commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Guard senior general, made Left Dragon Martial commander, then Zhaoyi military governor, then again Left Dragon Martial commander.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，遷左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was moved to Left Awesome Guard senior general.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 2 he was moved to Left Awesome Guard senior general.

sentences.zh: 數請老，不許。

translations.literal: Several times he asked to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Several times he asked to retire; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十五，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy-five and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five, posthumously Grand Preceptor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 張希崇

translations.literal: Zhang Xichong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xichong

sentences.zh: 張希崇，字德峰，幽州薊人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xichong, style name Defeng, was a man of Ji in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xichong, style name Defeng, came from Ji in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少好學，通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and mastered the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 劉守光不喜儒士，希崇因事軍中為偏將，將兵戍平州。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang disliked scholars; Xichong therefore entered the army as a deputy commander and led troops to garrison Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang disliked scholars. Xichong entered the army as deputy commander and garrisoned Ping.

sentences.zh: 其後契丹攻陷平州，得希崇，知其儒者也，以為盧龍軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Later the Khitan took Ping and seized Xichong; knowing he was a scholar, they made him acting chief of staff of the Lulong army.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Khitan took Ping and seized Xichong. Knowing him a scholar, they made him acting Lulong chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，盧文進自平州亡歸，契丹因以希崇代文進為平州節度使，遣其親將以三百騎監之。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong Lu Wenjin fled from Ping back south; the Khitan therefore had Xichong replace Wenjin as Ping military governor and sent a trusted general with three hundred horse to oversee him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong Lu Wenjin fled Ping south. The Khitan put Xichong in Wenjin’s place as Ping military governor and sent a trusted general with three hundred horse to watch him.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，虜將喜其為人，監兵稍怠，希崇因與其麾下謀走南歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year the barbarian general took to his character, the overseers grew slack, and Xichong with his men plotted to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the Khitan general took to him, oversight slackened, and Xichong and his men plotted flight south.

sentences.zh: 其麾下皆言兵我，不可俱亡，懼不得脫，因勸希崇獨去。

translations.literal: His men all said the troops were few and they could not flee together, fearing they would not escape, and urged Xichong to go alone.
translations.idiomatic: His men said their troops were few and they could not flee together—they feared capture—and urged Xichong to go alone.

sentences.zh: 希崇曰：「虜兵守我者三百騎爾，烹其將，其兵必散走。

translations.literal: Xichong said: “The barbarian troops guarding us are only three hundred horse—boil their commander and the soldiers will scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong said: “Only three hundred horse guard us—boil their commander and the soldiers will scatter.

sentences.zh: 且平州去虜帳千餘里，使其聞亂而呼兵，則吾與汝等在漢界矣！

translations.literal: Moreover Ping is more than a thousand li from the barbarian court; if they hear trouble and call troops, we and you will already be on Han soil!
translations.idiomatic: Ping lies more than a thousand li from the Khitan court. If they hear trouble and call troops, we will already be on Han soil!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆曰善。

translations.literal: ” All said it was good.
translations.idiomatic: ” All said it was good.

sentences.zh: 乃先為阱，置以石灰。

translations.literal: They first dug a pit and filled it with lime.
translations.idiomatic: They first dug a pit and filled it with lime.

sentences.zh: 明日，虜將謁希崇，希崇飲之以酒，殺之阱中，兵皆潰去，希崇率其麾下，得生口二萬南歸。

translations.literal: The next day the barbarian general called on Xichong; Xichong gave him wine to drink, killed him in the pit, the troops all scattered, and Xichong led his men with twenty thousand captives south.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the Khitan general called on Xichong. Xichong gave him wine, killed him in the pit, the troops scattered, and Xichong led his men with twenty thousand captives south.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘉之，拜汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Mingzong praised him and made him defense commissioner of Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong praised him and made him Ru defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷靈武節度使。

translations.literal: He was moved to military governor of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Lingwu military governor.

sentences.zh: 靈州地接戎狄，戍兵餉道，常苦抄掠，希崇乃開屯田，教士耕種，軍以足食，而省轉饋，明宗下詔褒美。

translations.literal: Ling’s territory bordered the Rong and Di; garrison grain routes were often harried by raids. Xichong opened military colonies, taught the soldiers to farm, the army had full food, and transport was saved; Mingzong issued an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Ling bordered the Rong and Di; supply routes were often raided. Xichong opened colonies, taught the men to farm, the army ate its fill, and transport was saved. Mingzong praised him by edict.

sentences.zh: 希崇撫養士卒，招輯夷落，自回鶻、瓜、沙皆遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Xichong comforted the soldiers and gathered the tribes; from the Uyghurs to Guazhou and Shazhou all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong comforted his soldiers and gathered the tribes. From the Uyghurs to Guazhou and Shazhou all sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 居四歲，上書求還內地，徙鎮邠寧。

translations.literal: After four years he memorialized asking to return to the interior and was shifted to govern Binning.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he asked by memorial to return inland and was shifted to Binning.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，復拜靈武節度使，希崇嘆曰：「吾當老死邊僥，豈非命邪！

translations.literal: When Jin’s Gaozu took the throne he was again made military governor of Lingwu; Xichong sighed: “Am I not fated to die old on the frontier margin!
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s Gaozu rose he was again made Lingwu military governor. Xichong sighed: “Am I not fated to die old on the frontier margin!

sentences.zh: 」希崇事母至孝，朝夕母食，必侍立左右，徹饌乃敢退。

translations.literal: ” Xichong served his mother with utmost filial piety; morning and evening at her meals he always stood at her side and only after the dishes were cleared dared withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xichong served his mother with utmost filial piety. Morning and evening at her meals he stood at her side and only after the dishes were cleared dared withdraw.

sentences.zh: 為將不喜聲色。

translations.literal: As a general he did not care for sound or color.
translations.idiomatic: As a general he cared nothing for sound or color.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，頗知星歷。

translations.literal: He loved reading and knew something of the stars.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and knew something of the stars.

sentences.zh: 天福三年，月掩畢口大星，希崇嘆曰：「畢口大星，邊將也，我其當之乎！

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu the moon occulted the great star at the Bi mouth; Xichong sighed: “The great star at the Bi mouth is a frontier general—I suppose it is for me!
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 3 the moon occulted the great star at the Bi mouth. Xichong sighed: “The Bi-mouth great star is a frontier general—is it meant for me!

sentences.zh: 」明年正月卒，贈太師。

translations.literal: ” The next year, in the first month, he died; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: ” He died the next first month and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 有子仁謙。

translations.literal: He had a son, Renqian.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Renqian.

sentences.zh: 相裏金

translations.literal: Xiang Lijin
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lijin

sentences.zh: 張廷蘊

translations.literal: Zhang Tingyun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyun

sentences.zh: 張廷蘊，開封襄邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Tingyun was a native of Xiangyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyun came from Xiangyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少為宣武軍卒，去事晉，稍遷軍校。

translations.literal: In youth he was a soldier of the Xuanwu army; he left to serve Jin and was gradually promoted to military cadet.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served the Xuanwu army, then went to Jin and rose by degrees to military cadet.

sentences.zh: 常從莊宗征伐，先登力戰，金瘡滿體，莊宗壯之，以為帳前黃甲二十指揮步軍都虞候、魏博三城巡檢使。

translations.literal: He often followed Zhuangzong on campaign, was first to climb and fought with all his strength; wounds of gold covered his body. Zhuangzong admired him and made him commander of the twenty companies of yellow armor before the tent, chief inspector of the step forces, and inspector of the three cities of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong on campaign, always first over the wall and fighting until wounds gilded his body. Zhuangzong admired him and made him commander of the twenty yellow-armor companies before the tent, chief inspector of the step forces, and inspector of Weibo’s three cities.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗在魏，以劉皇后從行，劉氏多縱其下擾人為不法，人無敢言者，廷蘊輒收而斬之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong was at Wei with Empress Liu accompanying him; the Liu clan often let their followers harass people unlawfully, and none dared speak—Tingyun would seize and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was then at Wei with Empress Liu in train. Her people often harassed the countryside and none dared protest—Tingyun seized and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 李繼韜叛於潞州，莊宗遣明宗為招討使，元行欽為都部署，廷蘊為馬步軍都指揮使，將兵為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Li Jitao rebelled at Luzhou, Zhuangzong sent Mingzong as pacification commissioner, Yuan Xingqin as overall deployer, and Tingyun as commander of the horse and foot forces, leading troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jitao rebelled at Luzhou. Zhuangzong sent Mingzong as pacification commissioner, Yuan Xingqin as overall deployer, and Tingyun to command horse and foot as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊至潞，日已暮，即率兵百餘逾濠登城，城守者不能禦，遂破潞州。

translations.literal: Tingyun reached Luzhou at dusk, at once led a hundred-odd men over the moat and onto the wall; the defenders could not hold him off, and Luzhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun reached Luzhou at dusk, took a hundred-odd men over the moat onto the wall, and broke the city—the garrison could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 明旦，明宗與行欽後至，明宗心頗慊之。

translations.literal: At dawn Mingzong and Xingqin arrived afterward; Mingzong’s heart was rather rankled.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong and Xingqin came at dawn after him; Mingzong was rankled.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊以功遷羽林都指揮使、申懷沂三州刺史、金潁隴絳四州防禦團練使、左監門衛上將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit Tingyun was moved to commander of the Feathered Forest guard, prefect of Shen, Huai, and Yi, defense-and-training commissioner of Jin, Ying, Long, and Jiang, and senior general of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For the exploit he became commander of the Feathered Forest guard, prefect of Shen, Huai, and Yi, defense commissioner of Jin, Ying, Long, and Jiang, and senior general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 開運中，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyun era he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊武人，所識不過數字，而平生重文士。

translations.literal: Tingyun was a man of war who knew barely a handful of characters, yet all his life he honored men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun was a fighting man who knew scarcely a handful of characters, yet he honored scholars all his life.

sentences.zh: 嘗從明宗破梁鄆州，獲判官趙鳳，廷蘊謂曰：「吾視汝貌必儒人，可無隱也。

translations.literal: Once, following Mingzong in taking Liang’s Yan Prefecture, he captured the judge Zhao Feng. Tingyun said to him: “By your looks you must be a Confucian—hide nothing from me.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Mingzong took Liang’s Yan Prefecture, he captured the judge Zhao Feng. Tingyun told him: “You look a scholar to me—hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 」鳳以實對，廷蘊亟薦於明宗。

translations.literal: ” Feng answered truthfully, and Tingyun at once recommended him to Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: ” Feng told the truth; Tingyun promptly recommended him to Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 後鳳貴為相，數薦廷蘊於安重誨，重誨屢言之，明宗以廷蘊破潞之隙，終恨之，故終不秉髦節。

translations.literal: Later, when Feng rose high as chief minister, he repeatedly recommended Tingyun to An Chonghui; Chonghui spoke for him again and again, but Mingzong, because of the Luzhou affair, bore a grudge to the end and therefore never gave him a commissioner’s banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng rose to chief minister he repeatedly urged Tingyun on An Chonghui, and Chonghui spoke for him again and again—but Mingzong still resented the Luzhou coup and never gave him a commissioner’s banner.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊素廉，歷七州，卒之日，家無余貲。

translations.literal: Tingyun was always frugal; through seven prefectures, on the day he died his house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun lived frugally. Through seven prefectures he held, his house had nothing left when he died.

sentences.zh: 馬全節

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanjie

sentences.zh: 馬全節，字大雅，大名元城人也。

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie, styled Daya, was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanjie, styled Daya, came from Yuancheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 唐同光中，全節為捉生指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era of Tang, Quanjie was commander of the captive-recruiting corps.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang’s Tongguang reign he commanded the captive-recruiting corps.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮反鄴都，以全節為馬步軍指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled at the Ye capital, Quanjie was made commander of the horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rebelled at the Ye capital, Quanjie was made commander of the horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，歷博單郢沂四州刺史、金州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Quanjie served in turn as prefect of Bo, Shan, Ying, and Yi and as defense commissioner of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Quanjie governed Bo, Shan, Ying, and Yi in turn and became defense commissioner of Jin.

sentences.zh: 廢帝時，蜀人攻金州，州兵才數百，全節散家財，與士卒堅守，蜀人去，廢帝召全節，以為滄州留後。

translations.literal: Under the deposed emperor, Shu attacked Jin; the prefectural troops numbered only a few hundred. Quanjie spent his household wealth and held firm with the soldiers; Shu withdrew. The deposed emperor summoned Quanjie and made him acting military governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor, Shu struck Jin with only a few hundred defenders. Quanjie spent his household wealth and held with his men until Shu withdrew. The court summoned him and made him acting governor of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，即拜全節橫海軍節度使，徙鎮安遠，代李金全。

translations.literal: When the Jin Founding Emperor took the throne, Quanjie was at once made military governor of the Transoceanic army and moved to secure Anyuan, replacing Li Jinquan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin Founding Emperor took the throne, Quanjie was made Transoceanic military governor, then moved to Anyuan in Li Jinquan’s place.

sentences.zh: 金全叛附於李，高祖發兵三萬，使全節與安審暉討之，金全南奔。

translations.literal: Jinquan rebelled and went over to Li; the Founding Emperor sent thirty thousand troops and had Quanjie and An Shenhui campaign against him. Jinquan fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan rebelled and joined Li. The Founding Emperor sent thirty thousand men; Quanjie and An Shenhui pursued until Jinquan fled south.

sentences.zh: 將李承裕守安州，全節與承裕戰州南，大敗承裕，斬首三千級，生擒千餘人。

translations.literal: The general Li Chengyu held An Prefecture. Quanjie fought Chengyu south of the prefecture, routed him utterly, beheaded three thousand, and took more than a thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Chengyu held An Prefecture. Quanjie met him south of the city, shattered his army, took three thousand heads, and captured more than a thousand alive.

sentences.zh: 承裕棄城去，審暉追至雲夢，執承裕及其兵二千人，全節斬千五百人，以其餘兵並承裕獻於京師。

translations.literal: Chengyu abandoned the city and fled. Shenhui pursued to Yunmeng, seized Chengyu and two thousand of his troops; Quanjie beheaded fifteen hundred, sent the rest of the troops with Chengyu to the capital as prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyu abandoned the city. Shenhui ran him down at Yunmeng with two thousand men. Quanjie beheaded fifteen hundred and sent the rest, with Chengyu, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 承裕謂全節曰：「吾掠城中，所得百萬計，將軍皆取之矣。

translations.literal: Chengyu said to Quanjie: “When I plundered the city I took a million in goods—and you took it all.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyu told Quanjie: “I looted the city for a million in goods—and you took every bit.

sentences.zh: 吾見天子，必訴此而後就刑。

translations.literal: When I see the Son of Heaven I shall surely plead this before I accept execution.
translations.idiomatic: Before I die I shall tell the Son of Heaven—and plead this first.

sentences.zh: 」全節懼，因殺承裕，高祖置而不問，徙全節鎮昭義。

translations.literal: ” Quanjie feared this and therefore killed Chengyu. The Founding Emperor let the matter pass and moved Quanjie to govern Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: ” Quanjie feared exposure and killed him. The Founding Emperor ignored it and moved Quanjie to Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 又徙安國。

translations.literal: He was again moved to secure Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was then shifted to Anguo.

sentences.zh: 從杜重威討安重榮，以功徙鎮義武。

translations.literal: Following Du Chongwei in campaigning against An Chongrong, for merit he was moved to govern Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Du Chongwei against An Chongrong and, for merit, was moved to Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 自出帝與契丹交惡，全節未嘗不在兵間。

translations.literal: From the time the Last Emperor and the Khitan turned hostile, Quanjie was never out of the wars.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Last Emperor and the Khitan broke with each other, Quanjie was never off the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 開運元年，為行營都虞候，契丹與晉大軍相距澶、魏之間，全節別攻白團城，破之，虜七百人。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun 1 he was chief inspector of the field army. The Khitan and the great Jin army faced each other between Chan and Wei; Quanjie separately attacked White Round City, took it, and captured seven hundred of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 1 he was chief inspector of the field army. Khitan and Jin faced each other between Chan and Wei; Quanjie took White Round City on his own and captured seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 克泰州，虜二千人，降其守將晉廷謙。

translations.literal: He took Taizhou, captured two thousand of the enemy, and received the surrender of its defending general Jin Tingqian.
translations.idiomatic: He took Taizhou, seized two thousand prisoners, and accepted the surrender of the defender Jin Tingqian.

sentences.zh: 四月，契丹敗於戚城，引兵分道而北，全節敗之於定豐，執其將安暉。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Khitan were defeated at Weicheng and withdrew north by separate routes; Quanjie defeated them at Dingfeng and seized their general An Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Khitan lost at Weicheng and split north. Quanjie beat them at Dingfeng and took their general An Hui.

sentences.zh: 七月，徙廣晉尹，留守鄴都。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was moved to mayor of Guangjin and left to guard the Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he became mayor of Guangjin and stayed to guard the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，杜重威為招討使，以全節為副，大敗契丹於衛村。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Du Chongwei was pacification commissioner; Quanjie was his deputy and inflicted a great defeat on the Khitan at Weicun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Du Chongwei led the campaign with Quanjie as deputy; together they crushed the Khitan at Weicun.

sentences.zh: 全節為人謙謹，事母至孝，其臨政決事，必問法如何。

translations.literal: Quanjie was modest and careful, filial toward his mother to the utmost; in governing and deciding affairs he always asked what the law required.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie was modest and careful, utterly filial to his mother, and in every decision asked what the law required.

sentences.zh: 初，徙廣晉，過元城，衣白襕謁其縣令，州裏以為榮。

translations.literal: When he was first moved to Guangjin and passed Yuancheng, he wore white robes to call on the county magistrate—the district took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: On his first move to Guangjin he passed Yuancheng in white robes to pay respects to the county magistrate—the district took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，徙鎮順國，未至而卒，年五十五，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun 2 he was moved to govern Shunguo; before he arrived he died, aged fifty-five, and was posthumously made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 2 he was ordered to Shunguo, died on the road at fifty-five, and was posthumously made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 皇甫遇

translations.literal: Huang Fuyu
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fuyu

sentences.zh: 皇甫遇，常山真定人也。

translations.literal: Huang Fuyu was a native of Zhending in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fuyu came from Zhending in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 為人有勇力，虬髯善射。

translations.literal: As a man he had courage and strength, a bristling beard, and skill in archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was strong and brave, wore a bristling beard, and shot well.

sentences.zh: 少從唐明宗征伐，事唐為武勝軍節度使，所至苛暴，以誅斂為務，賓佐多解官逃去，以避其禍。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Tang’s Mingzong on campaign. Serving Tang, he was military governor of the Wusheng army; wherever he went he was harsh and violent, making extortion his business, and many aides resigned and fled to escape his harm.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he campaigned under Tang’s Mingzong. As Wusheng military governor he was harsh wherever he went, lived by extortion, and aides fled his court in droves.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，歷義武、昭義、建雄、河陽四鎮，罷為神武統軍。

translations.literal: Under the Jin Founding Emperor he held Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Jianxiong, and Heyang in turn, then was dismissed to command the Shenwu armies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin Founding Emperor he held Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Jianxiong, and Heyang, then was relieved to command the Shenwu armies.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，陷貝州，出帝以高行周為北面行營都部署，遇為馬軍右廂排陣使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded and took Bei Prefecture, the Last Emperor made Gao Xingzhou northern campaign deployer and Fuyu array-master of the right wing of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan invaded and took Bei Prefecture. The Last Emperor made Gao Xingzhou northern deployer and Fuyu array-master of the horse army’s right wing.

sentences.zh: 是時，青州楊光遠據城反，出帝乃遣李守貞及遇分兵守鄆州。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Guangyuan of Qing Prefecture held the city in revolt; the Last Emperor then sent Li Shouzhen and Fuyu with divided troops to guard Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was in revolt behind his walls. The Last Emperor sent Li Shouzhen and Fuyu with split forces to hold Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遇等至馬家渡，契丹方將渡河助光遠，遇等擊敗之，以功拜義成軍節度使、馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Fuyu and the rest reached Majia Ford, the Khitan were about to cross the river to aid Guangyuan; Fuyu and the others defeated them and, for merit, Fuyu was made military governor of Yicheng and commander of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: At Majia Ford the Khitan were crossing to aid Guangyuan; Fuyu beat them off and was made Yicheng military governor and commander of the horse army.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，契丹寇西山，遣先鋒趙延壽圍鎮州，杜重威不敢出戰。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun 2 the Khitan raided the western hills; their vanguard Zhao Yanshou besieged Zhen Prefecture, and Du Chongwei dared not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 2 the Khitan raided the western hills. Zhao Yanshou besieged Zhen Prefecture while Du Chongwei would not fight.

sentences.zh: 延壽分兵大掠，攻破欒城、柏鄉等九縣，南至邢州。

translations.literal: Yanshou divided his troops for wide plunder, took Luan City, Baixiang, and eight other counties, and pushed south to Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou split his force to loot, took Luan, Baixiang, and eight other counties, and pressed south to Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是時歲除，出帝與近臣飲酒過量，得疾，不能出征，乃遣北面行營都監張從恩會馬全節、安審琦及遇等禦之。

translations.literal: It was year’s end; the Last Emperor drank too much with close ministers, fell ill, and could not take the field. He sent northern campaign overseer Zhang Congen to join Ma Quanjie, An Shenqi, and Fuyu to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At year’s end the Last Emperor drank too deep with his intimates, fell ill, and could not march. He sent Zhang Congen as northern overseer with Ma Quanjie, An Shenqi, and Fuyu to meet the raid.

sentences.zh: 從恩等至相州，陣安陽河南，遣遇與慕容彥超率數千騎前視虜。

translations.literal: Congen and the rest reached Xiang Prefecture, formed line south of the Anyang River, and sent Fuyu with Murong Yanchao at the head of several thousand horse to scout the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Congen reached Xiang Prefecture, drew up south of the Anyang, and sent Fuyu and Murong Yanchao ahead with several thousand horse to scout.

sentences.zh: 遇渡漳河，逢虜數萬，轉戰十餘里，至榆林，為虜所圍，遇馬中箭而踣，得其仆杜知敏馬，乘之以戰。

translations.literal: Fuyu crossed the Zhang River, met tens of thousands of the enemy, fought for more than ten li to Yulin, and was surrounded. Fuyu’s horse took an arrow and fell; he took his groom Du Zhimin’s horse and fought on it.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu crossed the Zhang, met tens of thousands, and fought ten li to Yulin before the enemy ringed him. His horse took an arrow and dropped; he seized his groom Du Zhimin’s mount and fought on.

sentences.zh: 知敏為虜所擒，遇謂彥超曰：「知敏，義士也，豈可失之！

translations.literal: Zhimin was captured by the enemy. Fuyu said to Yanchao: “Zhimin is a man of honor—how can we lose him!
translations.idiomatic: The enemy took Zhimin. Fuyu told Yanchao: “Zhimin is a man of honor—we cannot leave him!

sentences.zh: 」即與彥超躍馬入虜，取之而還。

translations.literal: ” He and Yanchao at once spurred into the enemy, seized him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: ” He and Yanchao charged into the enemy, pulled him out, and rode back.

sentences.zh: 虜兵與遇戰，自午至未，解而復合，益出生兵，勢甚盛。

translations.literal: The enemy fought Fuyu from the hour of horse to the hour of sheep; they broke off and closed again, sent out fresh troops, and their force grew very strong.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fought him from noon to mid-afternoon, broke, closed again, and fed in fresh troops until their press grew overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 遇戒彥超曰：「今日之勢，戰與走爾，戰尚或生，走則死也。

translations.literal: Fuyu warned Yanchao: “Today’s situation is fight or flee—fight and you may yet live; flee and you die.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu warned Yanchao: “Today it is fight or run—fight and you may live; run and you die.

sentences.zh: 等死，死戰，猶足以報國。

translations.literal: If we must die alike, die fighting—you may still repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: If death is the same either way, die fighting—you may still repay the state.

sentences.zh: 」張從恩與諸將怪遇視虜無報，皆謂遇已陷虜矣。

translations.literal: ” Zhang Congen and the generals thought it strange that Fuyu, scouting the enemy, sent no report, and all said Fuyu had already fallen to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congen and the other generals wondered why Fuyu sent no word from his scout and assumed he was lost.

sentences.zh: 已而有馳騎報遇被圍，安審琦率兵將赴之，從恩疑報者詐，不欲往，審琦曰：「成敗天也，當與公共之，雖虜不南來，吾屬失皇甫遇，復何面目見天子！

translations.literal: Then a rider galloped in reporting that Fuyu was surrounded. An Shenqi was about to lead troops to his aid; Congen suspected the report was a trick and would not go. Shenqi said: “Success and failure are Heaven’s—yet we must share it with the commander. Even if the enemy does not come south, if we lose Huang Fuyu what face have we to see the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: A rider then reported Fuyu surrounded. An Shenqi was about to march; Congen thought it a ruse and held back. Shenqi said: “Fortune is Heaven’s—but we must share it. Even if the Khitan never come south, lose Huang Fuyu and what face have we before the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」即引騎渡河，諸軍皆從而北，拒虜十餘里，虜望見救兵來，即解去。

translations.literal: ” He led horse across the river; all the armies followed north, held the enemy for more than ten li, and when the enemy saw rescue coming they broke off.
translations.idiomatic: ” He forded with his horse; the whole host followed north, held them ten li, and at sight of rescue the enemy drew off.

sentences.zh: 遇與審琦等收軍而南，契丹亦皆北去。

translations.literal: Fuyu and Shenqi and the rest gathered the army and withdrew south; the Khitan likewise all went north.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu, Shenqi, and the rest gathered their men and fell back south; the Khitan too marched north.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹兵已深入，人馬俱乏，其還也，諸將不能追，而從恩率遇等退保黎陽，虜因得解去。
