translations.literal: By then the Khitan army had driven deep in; men and horses were both spent. On their return the generals could not pursue, while Congen led Fuyu and the rest back to hold Liyang, and the enemy thus got away.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were deep in enemy country, men and horses spent. On the retreat no general pursued; Congen pulled Fuyu back to Liyang, and the enemy slipped away.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，以杜重威為都招討使，遇為馬軍右廂都指揮使，屯於中渡。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year Du Chongwei was overall pacification commissioner and Fuyu commander of the right wing of the horse army; they encamped at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third winter Du Chongwei was overall commander and Fuyu led the horse army’s right wing at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 重威已陰送款契丹，伏兵幕中，悉召諸將列坐，告以降虜，遇與諸將愕然不能對。

translations.literal: Chongwei had already secretly sent terms to the Khitan and hidden troops in his tent; he summoned all the generals to sit in a row and told them he would surrender to the enemy. Fuyu and the generals were stunned and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei had already secretly treated with the Khitan and hid troops in his tent. He called every general in, sat them in a row, and announced surrender. Fuyu and the rest were struck dumb.

sentences.zh: 重威出降表，遇等俯首以次自畫其名，即麾兵解甲出降。

translations.literal: Chongwei produced the surrender memorial; Fuyu and the rest bowed their heads and signed their names in turn, then he ordered the troops to lay down arms and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei produced the surrender memorial. Fuyu and the rest bowed and signed in turn, then Chongwei ordered arms stacked and the army surrendered.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣遇與張彥澤先入京師，遇行至平棘，絕吭而死。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Fuyu with Zhang Yanzhe to enter the capital first; when Fuyu reached Pingji he cut his throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Fuyu with Zhang Yanzhe ahead into the capital. At Pingji he cut his throat and died.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，梁亡而敬翔死，不得為死節；

translations.literal: Alas—when Liang fell Jing Xiang died, yet could not be called one who died for his integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Alas—when Liang fell Jing Xiang died, yet cannot be called a man who died for integrity;

sentences.zh: 晉亡而皇甫遇死，不得為死事，吾豈無意哉！

translations.literal: when Jin fell Huang Fuyu died, yet could not be called one who died in service—do I mean nothing by this!
translations.idiomatic: when Jin fell Huang Fuyu died, yet cannot be called a man who died in service—do I write for nothing!

sentences.zh: 梁之篡唐，用翔之謀為多，由子佐其父而弒其祖，可乎？

translations.literal: Liang’s usurpation of Tang relied largely on Xiang’s plans—a son aiding his father to murder his grandfather: can that be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s theft of Tang leaned on Xiang’s counsel—a son helping his father slay his grandfather: is that tolerable?

sentences.zh: 其不戮於斧鉞，為幸免矣。

translations.literal: That he was not cut down by axe and halberd was mere escape.
translations.idiomatic: That the axe never took him was only escape.

sentences.zh: 方晉兵之降虜也，士卒初不知，及使解甲，哭聲震天，即降豈其欲哉！

translations.literal: When the Jin troops surrendered to the enemy the soldiers at first did not know; when they were ordered to lay down armor, weeping shook heaven—is surrender what they wished!
translations.idiomatic: When Jin surrendered the ranks did not know at first; ordered to stack arms, they wept till heaven shook—was surrender their wish!

sentences.zh: 使遇奮然攘臂而起，殺重威於坐中，雖不幸不免而見害，猶為得其死矣，其義烈豈不凜然哉！

translations.literal: Had Fuyu suddenly flung up his sleeves, risen, and killed Chongwei in his seat—even if, unlucky, he could not escape harm—he would still have won a proper death; would not his fierce loyalty have stood blazing cold!
translations.idiomatic: Had Fuyu flung up his sleeves, risen, and killed Chongwei in his seat—even if harm could not be escaped—he would still have died as he ought; would not his fierce loyalty have stood ice-bright!

sentences.zh: 既俯首聽命，相與亡人之國矣，雖死不能贖也，豈足貴哉！

translations.literal: Once they bowed their heads and obeyed, together they destroyed another man’s state—even death cannot atone; how can it be prized!
translations.idiomatic: Once they bowed and obeyed they destroyed a state together—even death cannot atone; what is there to honor!

sentences.zh: 君子之於人，或推以恕，或責以備。

translations.literal: The gentleman toward men sometimes pushes with leniency, sometimes presses with strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Toward men the gentleman sometimes urges leniency, sometimes demands the strictest measure.

sentences.zh: 恕，故遷善自新之路廣；

translations.literal: Leniency—therefore the road to reform and renewal is wide;
translations.idiomatic: Leniency leaves the road to reform wide;

sentences.zh: 備則難得，難得，故可貴焉。

translations.literal: strictness is hard to win, and because it is hard to win, it is therefore precious.
translations.idiomatic: strictness is hard to earn, and because it is hard to earn, it is precious.

sentences.zh: 然知其所可恕，與其所可貴，豈不又難哉！

translations.literal: Yet to know what may be forgiven and what may be prized—is that not harder still!
translations.idiomatic: Yet to know whom to forgive and whom to prize—is that not harder still!

sentences.zh: 安彥威

translations.literal: An Yanwei
translations.idiomatic: An Yanwei

sentences.zh: 安彥威，字國俊，代州崞縣人也。

translations.literal: An Yanwei, styled Guojun, was a native of Guo County in Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An Yanwei, styled Guojun, came from Guo County in Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少以軍卒隸唐明宗麾下。

translations.literal: In youth, as a soldier, he entered service under Tang’s Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Tang’s Mingzong as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 彥威善射，頗知兵法。

translations.literal: Yanwei was skilled in archery and knew something of military method.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei shot well and knew some military method.

sentences.zh: 明宗鎮天平、宣武、成德，以彥威常為牙將，以謹厚見信。

translations.literal: When Mingzong held Tianping, Xuanwu, and Chengde, Yanwei was often a guard officer and was trusted for his care and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong governed Tianping, Xuanwu, and Chengde, Yanwei was often a guard officer and trusted for steadiness.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，皇子從榮鎮鄴，彥威為護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, the prince Congrong held Ye; Yanwei was commander of the Guarding-Sage corps.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Prince Congrong held Ye; Yanwei commanded the Guarding-Sage corps.

sentences.zh: 以從榮判六軍，彥威遷捧聖指揮使，領寧國軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Congrong was put in charge of the six armies, Yanwei was moved to commander of the Upholding-Sage corps and held the Ningguo military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong took the six armies, Yanwei became Upholding-Sage commander and Ningguo military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，拜彥威北京留守，徙鎮歸德。

translations.literal: When the Jin Founding Emperor took the throne, Yanwei was made northern capital regent and moved to govern Guide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin Founding Emperor took the throne, Yanwei became northern capital regent, then Guide military governor.

sentences.zh: 是時，河決滑州，命彥威塞之，彥威出私錢募民治堤。

translations.literal: At that time the Yellow River broke its banks at Hua Prefecture; Yanwei was ordered to block it and spent his private wealth to recruit people to repair the dike.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River then burst at Hua Prefecture. Ordered to stem it, Yanwei spent private funds to hire men for the dike.

sentences.zh: 遷西京留守，遭歲大饑，彥威賑撫饑民，民有犯法，皆寬貸之，饑民愛之，不忍流去。

translations.literal: Moved to western capital regent, he met a year of great famine; Yanwei relieved and comforted the starving. When the people broke the law he always pardoned them; the hungry loved him and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Made western capital regent in a year of famine, he fed and comforted the hungry, pardoned every petty crime, and the starving would not leave him.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過制。

translations.literal: On his mother’s death his grief exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died his grief exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 出帝與契丹隳盟，拜彥威北面行營副都統，彥威悉以家財佐軍用。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor broke the alliance with the Khitan, Yanwei was made deputy overall commander of the northern campaign; Yanwei spent all his household wealth on the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor broke with the Khitan, Yanwei became deputy northern commander and spent his whole household on the army.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒於京師。

translations.literal: He died of illness in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the capital.

sentences.zh: 彥威與安太妃同宗，出帝事以為舅，彥威未嘗以為言。

translations.literal: Yanwei was of the same clan as the Grand Consort An; the Last Emperor treated him as maternal uncle, yet Yanwei never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei shared clan with Grand Consort An; the Last Emperor treated him as uncle, yet Yanwei never mentioned it.

sentences.zh: 及卒，太妃臨哭，人始知同宗也，當時益稱其慎重。

translations.literal: When he died the Grand Consort came to mourn at his bier; only then did people learn they were kin, and at the time his discretion was praised all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the Grand Consort mourned at his bier—only then did people learn they were kin, and his discretion was praised the more.

sentences.zh: ○李瓊

translations.literal: ○ Li Qiong
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong

sentences.zh: 李瓊，滄州饒安人也。

translations.literal: Li Qiong was a native of Rao’an in Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong came from Rao’an in Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為騎將，與晉高祖隸唐明宗麾下。

translations.literal: In youth he was a cavalry officer and, with the Jin Founding Emperor, served under Tang’s Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a cavalry officer and, with the Jin Founding Emperor, served under Tang’s Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，契丹犯塞，明宗出涿州，遇契丹，與戰不勝，諸將各稍引去，而晉高祖獨戰不已，契丹漸合而圍之。

translations.literal: In Tongguang 2 the Khitan raided the frontier; Mingzong marched out of Zhuo Prefecture, met the Khitan, and fought without victory. The generals each gradually withdrew, but the Jin Founding Emperor alone kept fighting without cease as the Khitan gradually closed in and surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 the Khitan raided the frontier. Mingzong marched from Zhuo, met them, and lost. The generals peeled away one by one, but the Jin Founding Emperor fought on until the Khitan closed round him.

sentences.zh: 瓊引高祖衣與俱遁，至劉李河而追兵且及，瓊浮水先至南岸，高祖至河中流，馬踣，瓊以長矛援出之，又以所乘馬與高祖，而步護之，走十餘里，乃得免。

translations.literal: Qiong pulled the Founding Emperor’s robe and fled with him. They reached the Liu-Li River and pursuers were almost upon them. Qiong swam first to the south bank. The Founding Emperor reached midstream and his horse fell; Qiong used a long spear to pull him out, gave him the horse he rode, and on foot guarded him; after more than ten li they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong seized the Founding Emperor’s robe and ran with him. At the Liu-Li River pursuers were closing. Qiong swam to the south bank first. The Founding Emperor reached midstream, his horse went down; Qiong hauled him out on a long spear, gave him his own mount, and on foot guarded him ten li until they were safe.

sentences.zh: 明宗兵變於魏而南，瓊從高祖以三百騎先趨汴州。

translations.literal: When Mingzong’s army mutinied at Wei and marched south, Qiong followed Gaozu with three hundred horse and galloped ahead to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong’s troops mutinied at Wei and marched south, Qiong followed Gaozu with three hundred horse and raced ahead to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖為保義軍節度使，以為牙隊指揮使。

translations.literal: Gaozu was military governor of the Baoyi army and made him commander of the tooth guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was military governor of Baoyi and made him commander of the tooth guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖建國，以為護聖都虞候，賜與金帛甚厚，而不與之官爵，瓊亦郁郁。

translations.literal: When Gaozu founded the state he made Qiong chief adjutant of the Imperial Guard, gave gold and silks in great quantity, but granted no rank or title—and Qiong grew bitter.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu founded the state he made Qiong chief adjutant of the Imperial Guard and heaped gold and silks on him—but gave him no rank or title, and Qiong grew bitter.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜相、中二州刺史。

translations.literal: After long while he was appointed prefect of the two prefectures Xiang and Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made prefect of Xiang and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，為棣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Last Emperor’s time he was Di prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he was Di prefect.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠反，以書招瓊，瓊拒而不納。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan rebelled and recruited Qiong by letter; Qiong refused and would not join.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan rebelled and wrote to win Qiong over; Qiong refused and would not join.

sentences.zh: 遷洺州團練使，又為護聖右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was moved to militia commissioner of Mozhou and also made commander of the Imperial Guard’s right wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to militia commissioner of Mozhou and made commander of the Imperial Guard’s right wing.

sentences.zh: 晉亡，契丹入京師，以瓊為威州刺史，行至鄭州，遇盜見殺。

translations.literal: Jin fell; the Khitan entered the capital and made Qiong Wei prefect. At Zhengzhou bandits killed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell. Khitan entered the capital and made Qiong Wei prefect. On the road at Zhengzhou bandits killed him.

sentences.zh: 劉景巖

translations.literal: Liu Jingyan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingyan

sentences.zh: 劉景巖，延州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jingyan came from Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingyan came from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其家素富，能以貲交遊豪俊。

translations.literal: His family had long been rich and could use wealth to befriend bold men.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been wealthy and used money to befriend bold men.

sentences.zh: 事高萬金，為部曲，其後為丹州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Gao Wanjin as a household soldier and later became Dan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He served Gao Wanjin as a household soldier and later became Dan prefect.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖起兵太原，唐廢帝調民七戶出一卒為義兵。

translations.literal: When Jin’s Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan, Tang’s deposed emperor levied one soldier from every seven households as loyalist militia.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan, Tang’s deposed emperor drafted one soldier from every seven households as loyalist militia.

sentences.zh: 延州節度使楊漢章發鄉民赴京師，將行，景巖遣人激怒之，義兵亂，殺漢章，迎景巖為留後。

translations.literal: Yanzhou military governor Yang Hanzhang mobilized the countryside for the capital. As they were about to march, Jingyan sent men to inflame them; the militia rioted, killed Hanzhang, and welcomed Jingyan as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou military governor Yang Hanzhang mobilized the countryside for the capital. As they were about to march, Jingyan sent men to stir them up. The militia rioted, killed Hanzhang, and welcomed Jingyan as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖即位，即拜景巖節度使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he at once appointed Jingyan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he at once made Jingyan military governor.

sentences.zh: 景巖從事熊，為人多智，陰察景巖跋扈難制，懼其有異心，欲以利愚之，因語景巖，以謂邊地不可以久安，為陳保名享利之策，言邠、涇多善田，其利百倍，宜多市田射利以自厚。

translations.literal: Jingyan’s staff officer Xiong was clever; he secretly saw Jingyan was overbearing and hard to control, feared he would turn disloyal, and wished to dull him with profit. He told Jingyan the frontier could not be held long, laid out a plan to keep reputation and enjoy profit, said Bin and Jing had much good land whose yield was a hundredfold, and that he ought to buy land widely and shoot for gain to enrich himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan’s staff officer Xiong was a clever man. He had long seen Jingyan was overbearing and hard to control, feared disloyalty, and wished to befuddle him with profit. He told Jingyan the frontier was no place to stay long, urged a plan to keep name and enjoy gain, said Bin and Jing had fine fields worth a hundredfold, and that he ought to buy land and speculate to enrich himself.

sentences.zh: 景巖信之，歲餘，其獲甚多。

translations.literal: Jingyan believed him; in a little over a year his gains were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan believed him. In a little over a year his gains were very great.

sentences.zh: 景巖使朝京師，乃言：「景巖不宜在邊，可徙之內地。

translations.literal: When Jingyan was sent to audience at the capital, [Xiong] said: “Jingyan should not stay on the frontier—he can be moved to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyan went to audience at the capital, Xiong said: “Jingyan should not stay on the frontier. Move him inland.

sentences.zh: 」乃移景巖邠州，入拜補闕，而景巖又徙鎮保義，居未幾，又徙武勝。

translations.literal: ” They moved Jingyan to Binzhou; he entered court as Remonstrance Official, then was transferred again to hold Baoyi, and after not long to Wusheng.
translations.idiomatic: ” They moved Jingyan to Bin, made him Remonstrance Official at court, then transferred him to hold Baoyi; before long he was moved again to Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 景巖乃悟為賣己，遂誣奏隱己玉帶，坐貶商州上津令。

translations.literal: Jingyan then realized he had been sold out and memorialized falsely that Xiong had concealed his jade belt on him; Xiong was demoted to magistrate of Shangjin in Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan then saw he had been sold out and falsely memorialized that Xiong had hidden his jade belt; Xiong was demoted to magistrate of Shangjin in Shang.

sentences.zh: 懼景巖邀害之，道亡，匿山中。

translations.literal: Fearing Jingyan would waylay and harm him, he fled on the road and hid in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jingyan would ambush him, he fled on the road and hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 開運三年，景巖罷武勝，以太子太師致仕，居華州。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun year 3 Jingyan was removed from Wusheng, retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and lived at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun year 3 Jingyan left Wusheng, retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and lived at Hua.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯京師，以周密鎮延州，景巖乃還故里。

translations.literal: The Khitan attacked the capital; Zhou Mi was put over Yanzhou; Jingyan returned to his home country.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan attacked the capital. Zhou Mi was put over Yanzhou. Jingyan returned home.

sentences.zh: 而州人逐密，立高允權，允權妻劉氏，景巖孫女子也。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture drove off Mi and set up Gao Yunquan; Yunquan’s wife was the Liu clan—a granddaughter of Jingyan.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture drove Mi out and set up Gao Yunquan. Yunquan’s wife was a Liu—Jingyan’s granddaughter.

sentences.zh: 景巖良田甲第、僮仆甚盛，党項司家族畜牧近郊，尤富強，景巖與之往來，允權頗患之。

translations.literal: Jingyan had fine fields, grand houses, and many servants; the Tangut Si clan herded near the suburbs and were especially strong—Jingyan dealt with them back and forth, and Yunquan was much troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan had fine fields, grand houses, and many servants. The Tangut Si clan pastured near the suburbs and were especially strong; Jingyan kept company with them, and Yunquan was much troubled.

sentences.zh: 允權妻歲時歸省，景巖謂曰：「高郎一縣令，而有此州，其可保乎？

translations.literal: When Yunquan’s wife came home for yearly visits, Jingyan said to her: “Master Gao was only a county magistrate—can he hold this prefecture?
translations.idiomatic: When Yunquan’s wife came home on her yearly visit, Jingyan told her: “Master Gao was only a county magistrate—can he keep this prefecture?

sentences.zh: 」允權益惡之，而心又利其田宅，乃誣其反而殺之，年八十餘。

translations.literal: ” Yunquan hated him all the more, yet coveted his fields and houses; he charged him with rebellion and killed him, over eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yunquan hated him the more, yet coveted his land and houses. He charged him with rebellion and killed him, over eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 長子行琮，德州刺史，罷，留京師，亦被誅。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingcong, De prefect, had left office and stayed in the capital—he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingcong had been De prefect; dismissed, he stayed in the capital—and was executed too.

sentences.zh: 次子行謙，允權婦翁也，為奏言非劉氏子，遂免不誅。

translations.literal: The second son Xingqian, whose wife’s father was Yunquan, memorialized that he was not Liu’s son, and he was spared and not executed.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Xingqian—Yunquan was his father-in-law—memorialized that he was not of the Liu line, and he was spared execution.
